tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Primary shopping entry point. Use when a user wants to find, browse, compare, recommend, price-check, check availability of, shop for, or buy a physical product. Searches purchasable products across merchants participating in the Agent Checkout network. The user does not need to mention Agent Checko

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Legacy alias for search_products. Search purchasable products across participating merchants. Prefer search_products for new shopping requests.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get detailed product and variant information after search_products identifies a product and merchant. Use before purchase when the user needs details, options, price, or variant information.

tools.name: check_inventory
tools.description: Check whether a selected product variant is currently sellable and available. Use when availability matters or immediately before adding a selected variant to a cart.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Create a new Agent Checkout-attributed cart with a selected product variant. Use only after the user has chosen a specific product or clearly asked to add/buy it. This prepares the purchase but does not charge the buyer.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add another selected product variant to an existing Agent Checkout cart. Use when the user explicitly wants another item or quantity added to an existing cart. This does not charge the buyer.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the current Agent Checkout cart contents and totals. Use to review or confirm the cart before handing the buyer off to checkout.

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.description: Prepare the final buyer handoff by returning the merchant-hosted HTTPS checkout URL. Use when the user has a cart and clearly wants to proceed to checkout or purchase. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_checkout" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
